segments.text: What exactly is Enduroil?
But people keep mentioning it alongside Palantir, SpaceX and OpenAI.
But Enduroil is doing something very different.
WID is a defense technology company trying to rebuild military hardware around software, AI and autonomy.
Traditional defense companies build fighter jets, missiles, radars, ships and other huge weapons systems.
And those programs can take years, sometimes decades.
Enduroil's idea is what if defense hardware was built like modern technology products.
Faster development, more software, more autonomy, more iteration, and cheaper systems produced
at much larger scale.
The company was founded in 2017 by Par Malukki, the guy who founded Oculus before Facebook
acquired it, along with several co-founders.
In 2025 it reached a valuation of more than $30 billion, making it one of the most valuable
private defense technology companies.
But the most important part of Anduril is not one drone or one missile, it is the
software underneath, called Lattice.

Think of Lattice as an operating system for military hardware. Radars, cameras, drones, ground vehicles, underwater vehicles and other sensors normally come from different manufacturers and operate separately.
Lattice connects them. It takes data from thousands of sensors, combines it into one picture, identifies objects or threats and helps operators decide what happens next.
Now connect that software to Autonomous Hardware.
Anduril builds Ghost Drones, Roadrunner, Autonomous Aircraft, Fury,
a Fighter-style Autonomous Aircraft, Barracuda,
a family of cruise missile-like systems,
underwater vehicles like Dive and Copperhead,
and surveillance systems like Sentry.
So imagine Autonomous Drones monitoring an area.
One sensor detects something,
lattice identifies and tracks it,
then shares that with other systems.
A human operator supervises how they respond.
That is the core vision.
Not one person controlling one drone,
but one person supervising many autonomous systems working together.
Anduril calls this mission autonomy.
This is why AI matters so much.
A battlefield produces enormous amounts of data at once.
Camera feeds, radar, radio signals, locations, aircraft, drones.
No human can process all of that in real time.
So AI turns raw sensor data into answers.
What is this object? Where is it going?
Is it a threat? Which system can respond?
The other key part of Anduril's strategy is manufacturing.
Anduril argues that modern wars may require huge numbers of relatively affordable autonomous systems,
not a tiny number of incredibly expensive platforms.
So it is investing in arsenal, software-driven factories built to produce autonomous defence systems at much larger scale.
So the easiest way to think about Anduril is this.
Palantir helps defence organisations understand and use data.
SpaceX transformed how space hardware is built.
Anduril is trying to do something similar for defence.
Build the hardware, build the AI, build the software, connecting everything.
then manufacture it at scale.
It is turning military hardware from slow, manually operated machines
into a network of software-defined autonomous systems.
